title: A classification tool to foster self-regulated learning with generative artificial intelligence by applying self-determination theory: a case of ChatGPT
extended_summary:
This paper asks how ChatGPT, as a form of generative AI, can be used to support students’ self-regulated learning (SRL) and satisfy self-determination theory (SDT) needs from the perspective of school teachers. The study is positioned as a response to a gap in the literature: while generative AI is increasingly used in education, there is still limited clarity about which AI-supported learning activities help students’ autonomy, competence, relatedness, and SRL phases.

The authors used a Delphi design with 36 Hong Kong school teachers who had experience with technology-enhanced learning, SDT-based teaching, and ChatGPT-supported learning design. Across three rounds, participants reviewed, refined, combined, removed, and added candidate activities until consensus was reached. The panel represented several subjects, including English, Chinese, mathematics, science, humanities and art, and technology, and the schools covered different student levels in Hong Kong. The process produced a classification tool of 20 ChatGPT-based learning activities.

The main conclusion is that ChatGPT-based activities were seen as especially useful for supporting competence, followed by autonomy, while relatedness was least supported. The activities were also mapped to SRL phases, with performance and self-reflection supported more often than forethought. The paper concludes that ChatGPT can support SRL, but not fully on its own; teacher guidance remains important, especially in school settings. The resulting tool is intended to guide future research, classroom practice, and AI-in-education policy, but it is exploratory rather than an outcome study of student learning.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model chatbot for generating, revising, and discussing text and other content in a human-like, interactive manner.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the focal GenAI tool in a Delphi study to classify learning activities that school teachers believed could use ChatGPT to support self-regulated learning and satisfy SDT needs.

findings.finding_summary: Using a three-round Delphi with 36 Hong Kong school teachers, the study developed a classification tool of 20 ChatGPT-based learning activities that teachers agreed could support self-regulated learning. The paper does not report causal effects on student outcomes; it reports consensus patterns indicating ChatGPT was seen as especially useful for competence support, and less so for relatedness.
findings.measure: Teacher consensus on ChatGPT learning activities, mapped to SDT needs and SRL phases

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative Delphi consensus study, not a controlled trial or meta-analysis. It provides expert-derived classifications rather than outcome effects.
impact_tier_rationale: No effect size is reported and no student outcome was measured. The paper suggests potential utility for SRL support, but the impact is descriptive and unquantified.
